newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street's post-rout rebound proves shortlived.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street's post-rout rebound proves shortlived.

text.p: Wall Street's rebound from last Friday's rout proved short-lived as the market shed most of its early gains to show little change by midday Monday.

The Dow was calmer and likely to limp sideways at least until the "non-event" of Tuesday's Federal Reserve policy-making meeting, which was expected to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged, analysts said.
"It's a relief after the last five to six days," said Alfred Kugel, senior investment strategist at Stein Roe and Farnham.

The Dow was off 6.27 points or 0.08 percent, at 7688.39, after reaching a high of 7732.98 earlier in the session. Declines modestly outnumbered advances. The Nasdaq composite was off 4.95 points, or 0.32 percent, at 1557.08.
On Friday, the Dow fell 247 points, a drop that was partly prompted by renewed concerns over earnings by blue-chip companies, particularly Gillette Co.
On Monday, another blue chip, Hewlett-Packard Co, posted earnings that were below analysts' expectations, and the electronics company's stock tumbled 3-7/16 to 62-3/4.
Shares on major overseas exchanges also fell Monday.

"I think the big declines in the overseas markets were probably more influenced by Friday's action than they are a harbinger of anything that's going to happen on our side," Kugel said. "We have gotten the people who were most anxious out."

The dollar rallied against the mark, extending its overnight gains as the prospect of a German interest rate hike faded. A slide by the dollar on Friday was part of the reason for the Dow's sell-off that day.
Early Monday afternoon, the long bond was up 9/32 to yield 6.53 percent.
The S&P 500 futures were up 3.20 points at 902.
Despite last Friday's heavy selloff, traders said fundamentals have not changed. The economy was still in good shape. "Nothing has really changed," a trader said.
Gillette Co was off 3-7/8 at 82, extending losses notched up Friday after the company said its 1997 earnings would come in at the low end of the range of analysts' estimates.
Geron Corp built on an advance that began Friday, when the stock price doubled after news of an advance in its cloning technology. The stock was up 2 at 16.
